page_title: QST: The Self-Hosted, Open Source Universal Assessment Platform

sources.entry: QST - Online assessment software. From a quick quiz on your phone to large scale, high stakes, proctored desktop testing, easy, secure and economical. (Demo, Source Code) GPL-2.0 Perl

summary.name: QST
summary.one_liner: QST is a self-hosted, open source (GPLv2) assessment platform for quizzes, exams, and surveys, with question banks, GradeBook, analytics, and proctored testing support.
use_cases: Running quizzes and exams for a school or university
Building and sharing question banks across platforms
Grading STEM math and chemistry answers automatically
Hosting multi-tenant assessments for many organizations on one server
Running surveys and skip-logic question flows
summary.what_it_does: QST is a web-based assessment system that you host yourself on Windows, Linux, or macOS, or in Docker via a community-made container. It supports multiple question types, including MCQ, multiple answer, matching, equation, true/false, short answer, essay, surveys, and branching, with auto-marking for objective items and manual grading for essays. A built-in GradeBook offers per-question statistics and CSV/JSON export. Questions can be imported and exported in QST XML, Word XML, Moodle XML, IMS QTI 1/2/3, and PDF formats, and a visual editor creates MathJax/TeX/MathML equations without requiring LaTeX knowledge.
notable: Multi-tenant design: one server supports unlimited organizations, classes, and users
Visual STEM equation editor with MathJax/TeX/MathML/mhchem and auto-marking of equation answers
Imports and exports IMS QTI 1/2/3, Moodle XML, and Word XML for avoiding vendor lock-in
Distributed as a single QST.pm file under GPLv2 with mod_perl multi-threading
caveats: The page says it is not a full LMS, so it covers assessments rather than course delivery
AI question creation relies on a separate community GitHub project, and the Docker container is also a community creation
Proctored desktop testing is mentioned in the headline, but the page gives few details on how it works
